broken.reason: A2 prompt/oracle contradiction. The prompt's ONLY behavioural statement is the buggy code it prints, `assign out = (~sel & a) | (sel & b);`, which selects b when sel=1. The hidden golden is `assign out = sel ? a : b;`, which selects a when sel=1. The prompt asks to 'find the bug and fix this 8-bit wide 2-to-1 mux' -- the one defect its own text admits is the 1-bit `output out` declaration on an 8-bit mux. Repairing exactly that width defect and changing nothing else mismatches the golden in 111 of 114 samples: the golden inverts a select polarity the prompt fixes.

A2 prompt/oracle contradiction. The hidden golden drives `mux_in[2] = ~d`. As a function of (c,d) that is (1,0,1,0); NO column of the K-map printed in the prompt has that function. Since the four mux_in indices can only be a bijection onto the four printed columns, all 4! = 24 index mappings are excluded at once. The single contradicted cell is ab=10, cd=11, where the printed map says 1 and ~d gives 0.
